#### Round 3

The terminal-event fix is implemented. All nine focused EOF/exit recovery tests
and the Codex channel-lifetime assertion pass. Formatting, Clippy, `vp check`,
and all 11 workspace typecheck tasks pass. `vp check` retains 442 existing
warnings; unchanged Effect language-service suggestions are included below.

The full Rust selections remain blocked by sandbox listener/hook restrictions:
127/132 unit tests and 121/143 integration tests pass. Both selections were
retried with the same failure sets. Live SIGKILL/Send now verification requires
the host. The pre-terminal-notification delivery race remains explicitly
documented below.

The host confirmed Round 2 and the graceful-restart scenario, but a real Codex
process loss still reused its dead driver. The prior fixtures ended their event
channels; Codex retains its sender after publishing failure and `session.exited`.
This round fixes that distinction in the supervisor only. The coordinator's
semaphore-fixture sender retention is preserved, as are all unrelated changes.
No commit or dependency change is made.

The host correction also identified the semaphore case as the same dropped-sender
fixture regression. Its corrected sender lifetime is retained byte-for-byte.

Implementation and test evidence:

- `spawn_event_pump` now treats a fatal `session.exited` for its own thread and
  EOF as the same terminal condition. It still projects the exit event normally,
  then performs one shared activity/turn settlement, cancellation, driver
  shutdown, and return. No provider runtime implementation closes its channel as
  part of this fix; the Codex runtime file contains a test-only assertion.
- The existing `SessionStreamEnded` coordination starts before exit projection
  becomes visible, after activity-control acknowledgements that can call back
  into the supervisor. The Round 2 timeout, retained completion receiver, and
  retry/rejection policy remain in use. This avoids creating an acknowledgement
  cycle while protecting delivery during the final projection.
- Synthetic failure is conditional on a remaining `active_turn_id`. The prior
  EOF block read that ID but synthesized failure even when it was absent; the
  requested guard is now explicit. A native failed turn followed by exit retains
  its exact error message and class, with one error-session projection and one
  projected exit activity. An exit with an active turn still receives the existing
  synthetic transport failure and assistant settlement.
- New regression cases emit failed-turn then exit while retaining the sender,
  and exit without a preceding settle. Both failed before the change and now
  verify replacement launch, delivery acceptance, native resume identity, and
  steer rejection without relaunch. EOF cases remain. Additional coverage checks
  exit-projection fencing and OpenCode's explicit-stop exclusion. The existing
  Codex transport-close test now verifies that `next_event()` remains pending
  after the two native terminal events; no native runtime behavior changed.

Provider emission audit (current source, not inferred from channel lifetime):

| Provider | Terminal source and intentional-operation check                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| -------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Codex    | `provider/codex/runtime.rs::handle_incoming` emits failed completion for the active turn, then `session.exited`, on `IncomingEvent::Closed`. Both the handler entry and close branch check `explicit_close`; `shutdown` sets it before stopping the reader. Interrupt sends `turn/interrupt` and does not close the session. The runtime retains `events_tx`, confirmed by the runtime-level assertion.                                                                    |
| Claude   | `provider/claude/runtime.rs::handle_stream_failure` emits `session.exited` with reason `stream_failure`, which denotes loss of the stream. In this checkout that canonical helper is called only by tests; the production `spawn_claude_output` path cancels its forwarding tasks on stdout EOF and can reach ordinary EOF instead. Ordinary interrupt stops turn input and writes the interrupt control request; it does not call the stream-failure helper or emit exit. |
| Cursor   | `provider/cursor/runtime.rs::handle_incoming` emits exit only for ACP `IncomingEvent::Closed`; ordinary interrupt sends `session/cancel`. The raw adapter can observe a close when intentional shutdown kills the child, but the supervisor has already canceled and joined its event pump, so that notice cannot enter loss recovery. There is no legitimate live-session exit notification.                                                                              |
| Grok     | The corresponding ACP close handler is the sole exit emitter; interrupt sends `session/cancel`. Intentional driver shutdown has the same supervisor cancellation ordering as Cursor. The current provider kill switch is unchanged; this is a source audit of its existing runtime.                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| OpenCode | Both sites were checked: `stop()` emits `Session stopped.` intentionally, while clean SSE EOF emits `OpenCode closed its event stream.` for connection loss. The former is explicitly excluded from the new fatal-exit trigger. Connect/status/chunk failures also end the runtime event stream and remain covered by EOF handling. Turn interrupt posts to `/session/{id}/abort` and emits no exit itself.                                                                |

For every provider, normal session stop and idle suspension go through
`detach_session`, which cancels and joins the supervisor event pump before
`driver.shutdown()`. Thus raw shutdown notices cannot be projected as unexpected
loss. OpenCode additionally has the explicit reason exclusion above; there was
no reason to change five native channel implementations or implement both
alternative approaches.

Provider architecture and the shared validation runbook now name fatal
`session.exited` or EOF as the trigger, require a sender-open native sequence in
fixtures, and cover preservation of a pre-existing turn failure. The runbook was
reviewed and updated. No React code changed; the existing recovery flow still
preserves queued work and lets the user choose Send now.

Review boundary: the supervisor can only retire a driver after observing its
terminal event. A send while the preceding failed-turn event is still being
projected, before `session.exited` is consumed, can still reach Codex and receive
the existing ambiguous-delivery outcome. This predates this diff; it is recorded
as a remaining notification race, not claimed fixed by the terminal-event rule.
The read-only review found no actionable issue in the requested Round 3 change.

CodeGraph sync again exited 1 during parsing without a diagnostic. Its graph was
treated as unavailable; source, tests, manifests, and existing documentation were
used directly. Full validation output follows. ANSI color escapes and trailing
or surrounding whitespace are normalized for Markdown; no diagnostic or result
lines are omitted. Commands run from `/work/workspaces/orca/BibCode/main-3` and
capture stdout/stderr together with `tee` and `pipefail`.

Formatting and Clippy passed. The focused terminal recovery group passed 9/9,
including four new exit-event regressions and the retained EOF/timeout cases.
The additional Codex runtime assertion passed in its existing test (0.01 s).

The full provider-runtime unit selection ran twice with 127 passed / 5 failed.
These are the same restricted native cases as Round 2: OpenCode cannot bind its
fixture listener, and four Claude targeted-control tests lose hook capability
when their hook listener cannot start (so the expected request capture is absent
or the operation is unsupported). The standalone socket probe again confirms
`PermissionError: [Errno 1] Operation not permitted` at socket creation.

The integration suite reports 121 passed / 22 failed. Its failures are the same
listener/hook-dependent cases seen in Round 2; the new exit-event tests pass in
the full selection. The coordinator's semaphore fixture and the mixed-attachment
fixture both stop at listener creation here. This does not challenge the host's
green fixture results, and no assertions were weakened to accommodate the
sandbox. The exact selection is retried and all output is included below.

No live Codex SIGKILL/UI acceptance pass is claimed in this environment. The two
full Rust selections and the live scenario still need the host with local
listeners. Injected-failure warnings and the passing process fixture's
`kill: ... No such process` diagnostic remain in the captured output.
